extracted.intended_audience: prospective grantees, donors, researchers, and the general public interested in Carnegie Corporation's mission and funding priorities
extracted.subtask_description: This page describes Carnegie Corporation of New York's mission, historic principles, programmatic focus areas, geographic scope, and philanthropic approach that guide its grantmaking decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandate: advancement and diffusion of knowledge and understanding
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnegie Corporation was established to “promote the advancement and diffusion of knowledge and understanding.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation’s work is intended to align with this historic mandate; current activities emphasize education, knowledge, and scholarly approaches that advance understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Programmatic focus areas
rubrics_metrics.description: The Corporation currently supports four key program areas, including Education, Democracy, International Peace and Security, and Higher Education and Research in Africa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prospective work should clearly map to one or more of these program areas; these represent primary topical priorities for funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority issues: education, democracy, and international peace
rubrics_metrics.description: The foundation works to reduce political polarization through philanthropic support for issues Carnegie considered most important: education, democracy, and peace.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programs that target reduction of polarization, strengthen democratic institutions, advance education, or promote peace are aligned with Carnegie’s stated priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geographic scope and specific regional focus
rubrics_metrics.description: The Corporation is headquartered in New York City, but grantmaking is both national and international in scope. While Carnegie’s primary aim was to benefit the people of the United States, it also supports selected countries in sub-Saharan Africa (notably under Higher Education and Research in Africa).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should note that Carnegie funds both U.S. and international work and that some program areas have explicit regional emphases (e.g., selected sub‑Saharan African countries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on long-term, sustainable impact ('real and permanent good')
rubrics_metrics.description: Carnegie dedicated the foundation to doing “real and permanent good in this world” and creating “ladders on which the aspiring can rise.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grant proposals that demonstrate durable, systemic benefits and pathways for upward mobility or sustained improvement align with this principle; preference for interventions with lasting positive effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific philanthropy / evidence- and scholarship-based approaches
rubrics_metrics.description: Through more than a century of grantmaking, the Corporation has applied the principles of “scientific philanthropy” — working with the best ideas and cutting‑edge strategies that draw strength from deep knowledge and scholarship.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals should be grounded in rigorous evidence, scholarship, or tested approaches; innovation that is informed by research and intellectual rigor is encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexibility and trustee authority to respond to changing needs
rubrics_metrics.description: Andrew Carnegie granted trustees “full authority to change policies or causes hitherto aided, from time to time, when this, in their opinion, has become necessary or desirable,” acknowledging that “conditions upon the earth inevitably change.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The foundation reserves the right to adapt priorities over time; applicants should be aware that funding emphases may shift and should frame proposals to show relevance to current conditions and trustee priorities.
